ledger.note: November 1372: Nerio Acciaioli, lord of Corinth. Niccolo Acciaioli left Corinth to Angelo on 8 November 1365, who 'soon mortgaged it to Nerio, who settled in the town'; Philip of Taranto confirmed Angelo's hereditary right in 1371; 'Pope Gregory XI called Nerio lord of the town of Corinth' in November 1372, the first date on which the page names him lord.

Late 1374 or early 1375: Nerio takes Megara. 'With the support of Megara's burghers, Nerio captured the town and imprisoned its Catalan commander, Francis Lunel.' The Duchy page names Megara only as a diocese within the duchy.

1385: Nerio takes the lower town of Athens. 'Nerio's forces seized the lower town of Athens but failed to take the Acropolis'; a Venetian record of 7 July 1385 calls him 'ruler of Corinth and the Duchy of Athens'. He withdrew to Thebes from the Acropolis siege in the plague years 1386-87.

1385: Thebes (disputed). The page gives three accounts: Lock has Nerio capture Thebes from the Navarrese during the siege of the Acropolis in 1385; Setton has him buy it from Navarrese commanders after 1381; in 1379 Navarrese forces 'acting on Nerio's instigation' had taken it (June 1379). Bridging year: 1385, the page's only explicit year.
1388: the seat moves from Corinth to Athens, the infobox capital. The pages name no earlier capital; Nerio 'settled' in Corinth.

2 May 1388: Nerio's troops take the Acropolis. 'Nerio's troops captured the Acropolis, ending Catalan rule in Athens.' The Duchy page: 'when the Acciaioli family of Florence captured Athens' in 1388. The catalan-company dossier carries the matching loss.

1390: Nerio takes Neopatras. 'Before end of 1390: Nerio's forces captured Neopatras' (Nerio page); the Duchy page: 'Neopatras was occupied in 1390.' The catalan-company dossier carries the matching loss.
22 May 1390: Nerio cedes Megara to Venice. He 'ceded Megara to Venice during negotiations for his release' from Pedro de San Superano, who had seized him on 10 September 1389.

Late 1393: Bayezid I takes Neopatras. 'Bayezid I invaded Thessaly and captured Neopatras and Livadeia'; in early 1394 Nerio agreed to pay the sultan an annual tribute. Livadeia is in Nerio's will of 1394, so it is not dropped from Boeotia.
11 January 1394: Ladislaus of Naples invests Nerio I with the Duchy of Athens. Until then he was lord of Corinth and ruler of Athens; the Duchy page's list starts the Acciaioli dukes in 1388.

September 1394: Corinth leaves the Acciaioli. Bridging: Nerio died on 25 September 1394 and left Athens to the Church of Saint Mary (the Parthenon); 'Bartolomea claimed Corinth after Nerio's will favoured Francesca', and Carlo I Tocco sold Corinth and Megara to Theodore I in 1396 (Antonio page). The page does not say how or when Corinth left; Tocco is inferred from the 1396 sale.

18 March 1395: Venice annexes Athens. 'The Venetian Senate acknowledged the annexation of Athens'; the Duchy page: 'From 1395 to 1402 the Venetians briefly controlled the Duchy' (podestas Albano Contarini 1395-97, Nicolo Vitturi 1400-02). Antonio keeps the Boeotian castles.

First half of 1402: Antonio takes the lower town of Athens in a surprise attack. On 22 August 1402 the Senate ordered Francesco Bembo to invade Boeotia; Antonio ambushed and captured him before 2 September.
January or February 1403: the Acropolis surrenders. 'After refusing to make peace, he forced the Acropolis garrison to surrender.' A compromise of 31 March 1405 recognised his right to rule Athens.
1403: Antonio I restores the Acciaioli in Athens ('Antonio I (1402-1435), restored', Duchy page).

1456: the Ottomans take Athens but not the Acropolis. 'Turahanoglu Omer Bey conquered the remnants of the Duchy' in 1456 after the fall of Constantinople; Franco 'and the citizens held out on the Acropolis until June 1458' (Franco page). The Duchy infobox ends the state in 1458.
June 1458: the Acropolis surrenders. Franco and the citizens 'were forced to surrender'.
June 1458: Athens passes to the Ottomans; Mehmed II entered the city in August 1458 and let Franco keep Thebes 'as his vassal'.
August 1458: the dukes' seat moves from Athens to Thebes, where Mehmed II let Franco remain as his vassal.

1460: Franco dies and Thebes is annexed. Janissaries reported a plot to restore Franco in Athens; Zaganos Pasha summoned him to the Morea and told him his last hour had come. The page gives no month or annexation year beyond 'Annexed by Ottoman Empire'.

region.text: Thebes, which Mehmed II let Franco keep as his vassal after August 1458

ledger.note: 1460: the last Acciaioli duke is dead and the duchy is gone. The Duchy of Athens page ends the state in 1458 (infobox) with the conquest of the remnants in 1456; Franco's vassal Thebes lasts two more years.

wars.name: Acciaioli conquest of Athens
wars.outcome: Nerio took the lower town of Athens in 1385 and the Acropolis on 2 May 1388, ending Catalan rule in Athens; plague forced him to withdraw to Thebes in 1386-87.

wars.name: Bayezid I's invasion of Thessaly
wars.outcome: Bayezid captured Neopatras and Livadeia in late 1393; Nerio agreed in early 1394 to pay an annual tribute.
wars.note: Livadeia reappears in Nerio's September 1394 will, so it was recovered or never held; the page does not say.

wars.name: Venetian-Acciaioli struggle for Athens
wars.outcome: Venice annexed Athens in 1395 and held it to 1402; Antonio I took the lower town in 1402 and the Acropolis in early 1403; a compromise of 31 March 1405 recognised his rule.
wars.note: Antonio ambushed and captured Francesco Bembo in 1402; in 1406 he captured a Venetian bridgehead in Attica.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Duchy of Athens
wars.outcome: Turahanoglu Omer Bey conquered the remnants of the duchy in 1456; Franco held the Acropolis until June 1458; Mehmed II entered Athens in August 1458 and let Franco keep Thebes as a vassal until 1460.

certainty.note: No treaty line is on any page opened. Corinth, Megara and Neopatras are castellanies and towns with undefined hinterlands; Attica and Boeotia are the infobox's lands held and the Thessalian extension is not drawn.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row for the Acciaioli period. Slug is the one eu-05-c, eu-05-e and the catalan-company dossier already use. Four pages opened (Nerio I and Antonio I give the details the Duchy page lacks). Not settled: (1) the start: the Duchy page and the Catalan Company dossier date the Acciaioli duchy from Athens in 1388; this dossier starts at Nerio's lordship of Corinth (November 1372, the first page date) so that the Corinth loss in the Achaea dossier has a counterpart; the duchy title is Ladislaus's investiture of 11 January 1394; (2) Thebes in 1385 (three accounts); (3) how Corinth left the Acciaioli in 1394-96 (page silent); (4) the Argos and Nauplia lordship (1388: Nerio seized Nauplia, Theodore occupied Argos, Venice bought the lordship on 12 December 1388) belongs to a lordship-of-argos-and-nauplia dossier that is not written; (5) the 1444 tribute to Constantine Palaiologos is on the Duchy page and is recorded as a vassal event in the despotate-of-the-morea dossier; (6) the Ottoman tribute from early 1394 is for the Ottoman dossier (vassal events with counterpart acciaioli-duchy-of-athens). Navarrese Company still needs a dossier (named in eu-05-e's report).
